Slayer experience is typically gained when players kill varying amounts of monsters that are assigned to them by a Slayer Master.

It can also be trained in other ways, such as completing Soul Reaper assignments from Death or questing.

To gain the most Slayer points, though not necessarily the best Slayer experience per hour, you should obtain assignments from the highest level Slayer master that your combat level and Slayer level allow. The majority of Slayer masters give the same amount of points for completing an assignment regardless of what their assignment and your levels are, but a special case is The Raptor in Fort Forinthry, who scales with your level. Once your combat level is around 90, it is a good strategy to obtain assignments exclusively from The Raptor (you would otherwise use Sumona) until you unlock Kuradal (do not use The Raptor at very low levels as the points are poor). Switching to Kuradal at 110 combat level and 75 Slayer makes it more likely that you will receive assignments that can be completed in the nearby dungeon and therefore obtain drops like the ferocious ring, which will aid your training.

Slaying the monsters assigned by a higher-level Slayer master usually gives more Slayer experience, although this is not always the case, depending on what assignment is given. The experience is received for each monster killed while on an assignment; no extra experience is provided for completing a Slayer task. Different Slayer masters have their own set of monsters that they can give assignments for. These assignments are weighted, which determines the likelihood that a player will get a specific assignment. Some Slayer assignments are shared among multiple Slayer masters, but they may have different quantity ranges or task weights. If players have a preference for the monsters they'd like to slay for experience, it is reasonable to select a Slayer master that is more likely to assign those monsters.

Some players train Slayer using only one master. However, it is a common strategy to train Slayer by switching between two masters; one specific Slayer master that is appropriate for (or lower than) your level, and a higher-levelled Slayer master in order to take advantage of completion milestones. Every 10th and 50th task, players earn 5 and 15 times the Slayer master's standard amount of Slayer points. It is possible to complete the first 9 assignments with a low-level master and then switch to a higher-level master for the comparatively larger bonus. Higher-level masters will assign more difficult tasks than the typical Slayer Master would, either in monster assigned or quantity given, but the reward is a greater bonus of Slayer points.

Tasks assigned by Turael/Spria do not award Slayer points nor do they count towards the Slayer task count. Changing a task with Turael or Spria resets the task count to zero and, therefore, requires the player to complete another four assignments to start receiving points again.

Upon completing tasks assigned by Mandrith, the player will be awarded a Wilderness slayer chest. Without dying, killing outside the Wilderness, or skipping tasks, the player will also be awarded one Reaper point.

Slayer points are used to purchase various rewards from any of the Slayer Masters. It is highly recommended to complete the Smoking Kills quest as soon as possible to receive full Slayer points from assignments and challenges. Players who have not completed the quest will only receive half of the Slayer points per task.

When training Slayer for better experience rate, this is generally an optimal order for spending Slayer reward points:

  • Blocking assignments
  • Slayer helmet unlocking and upgrades
  • Preferring or extending assignments
  • Extra unlocks (such as rings of slaying)
  • Enabling the assignments of certain Slayer monsters

Slayer assignments can be blocked at any Slayer Master for 100 slayer points; this requires the player's current assignment be the creatures they wish to block. Up to eight assigned monsters, or group of monsters such as grotworms or mutated jadinkos, can be blocked in this manner, with one block allowed every 50 quest points.

Cancelling the assignment costs 30 points. The monster must be the currently assigned task for it to be cancelled. In order to maximise efficiency, players should cancel tasks which are commonly assigned yet offer slow rates of Slayer experience, often due to issues such as the inability to use a cannon and/or a titan, low life points, or other factors, such as long animations or specialised killing methods. Please see the assignment summary section below to determine which tasks should be considered for the use of a block.

Players are recommended to use the cancel option as often as it can be used while maintaining a stable level of Slayer points. This will ensure that the player spends as much time as possible doing tasks which offer fast Slayer experience.

The task summary section of this guide will tell you which tasks to block, which to skip, and which to complete if you are running low on Slayer points. For example, a player who is running low on points may do a greater demon task even though these tasks are usually cancelled. These tasks also give out more ferocious rings if done in Kuradal's Dungeon.

If a toggleable task is on that the player does not wish to do, toggle the task off, as it is essentially a pseudo-block.

Some assignments can be extended for Slayer points, which will greatly increase the number that you can slay if they give you that creature for a task. Only extend tasks that you generally do; it is a waste of points if you extend a task that you skip frequently or do not like.

Players can add many Slayer items to their tool belt, such as a rock hammer and some special items (charming imp, bonecrusher, herbicide, seedicide, advanced gold accumulator). The latter items require 500 slayer points each to be able to be added to the tool belt.

In general, use the best equipment available for the fastest rates. Additionally, power armour is more useful than tank armour. If available, always wear augmented gear when training Slayer.

Full slayer helmet variants are best-in-slot for any assignments. In order to make the slayer helmet, the player must have a myriad of slayer equipment; most can be bought from a Slayer Master, but the three core components - the black mask, hexcrest and focus sight, are instead acquired by killing cave horrors, jungle and desert strykewyrms respectively, requiring 73 Slayer. The necromancy equivalent, the spectral lens, is instead acquired from Profane Scabarites, requiring 87 Slayer. Unlike the other components, in order to add the spectral lens to the helmet, the player must additionally undergo an ensoul ritual requiring 80 Necromancy. If the player cannot make the helm for any reason, using the base component is instead recommended, but it is important to prioritise this upgrade immediately.

Cinderbane gloves are best-in-slot hand slot equipment for poisonable monsters. Most of the Slayer monsters are not immune to poison. The gloves can used with any weapon poison variants to amplify the poison damage. Otherwise, any power armour should be a replacement.

A demon horn necklace and its lesser variants in combination with a bonecrusher are best-in-slot neck slot equipment for slaying monsters that drop bones. The necklace restores prayer points when burying certain bones. In conjunction with an attuned ectoplasmator instead of bonecrusher, which monsters drop demonic ashes or are ghosts, the combination can quickly restore prayer points also, so that the players can keep prayers much longer without extra prayer restoration. After completing the quest Pieces of Hate, the holy wrench in the backpack or being worn boosts the amount of prayer points restored, but it occupies a backpack space or pocket slot.

A blood amulet of fury is great for recovering life points when slaying the monsters which do not drop bones and demonic ashes, or are not ghosts. If the player has access to Soul Split, the amulet is made more redundant since it can cover everything with proper flicking and improve damage output by slotting in a stronger amulet.

Luck rings are generally the best to use, as they offer bonuses to all combat styles, and increase the chance of getting a rare drop table drop or unique slayer monster drops.

The Vampyrism and Penance spells are ideal to use for low-intensity Slayer, by restoring life points and prayer points, respectively.

Recommended equipment list

Players should always use the style that their slayer assignment is weak to, with some exceptions which will be detailed in the slayer table.

Always use the highest level Slayer helmet that you have. If the slayer helmet stand is available, put the slayer helmet there. The benefits from the slayer helm become global once it is mounted there, allowing players to use better helmets with higher stats and/or set effects.

For all combat styles, two-handed weapons are preferred, as almost all area-of-effect abilities can be cast with two-handed weapons. For melee, halberd-type weapons are particularly effective for its AoE capabilities. For ranged, chinchompas, especially mechanised chinchompa, are particularly effective for its area-of-effect mechanics, when used in combat, it deals damage to all opponents in a 3x3 area around your target.

Some monsters are also susceptible to various weapons for additional damage and accuracy:

  • For melee-classed enemies, use the Inquisitor staff as it switches to tier 94–97 damage along with tier 89–92 accuracy
  • For magic-classed enemies, use the hexhunter bow as it switches to tier 94–97 damage along with tier 89–92 accuracy
  • For ranged-classed enemies, use the terrasaur maul as it switches to tier 94–97 damage along with tier 89–92 accuracy
  • Having the enchantment of affliction, enchantment of dispelling and enchantment of savagery increases the damage boost of above weapons from 12.5% to 17.5%.
  • For fighting any type of abyssal demon, use the abyssal bane 2h sword as its stats equivalent to a weapon with tier 100 damage and tier 79 accuracy.
  • For fighting certain demons, use the upgraded Darklight (using 5 silver pennies in Aris' Reward Shop after completion of the quest Dimension of Disaster), as its passive effects and special attacks greatly increase damage output against the demons.

The most essential piece of gear is the slayer helmet and its variants. It provides a 7.5-9.5% increase to damage and 12.5-14.5% increase to accuracy when slaying monsters on-task and incorporates all slayer headgear effects, including spiny helmet, face mask, earmuffs, nose peg.

Maximum of 5 fully charged ring of slaying and 6 fully charged ferocious rings can be stored in the slayer helmets with 60 Crafting and unlocking the ability for 500 Slayer points.

All slayer helmets can be stored on the slayer helmet stand in Anachronia base camp, granting its on-task damage and accuracy boost as a passive effect, allowing players to wear any style specific helmet. Ring of slaying and ferocious ring effects do not work with the helmet on the stand.

A cannon is another incredibly useful piece of equipment, which is often used to speed up tasks. The "Restocking Cannon" perk purchased from the Artisans' Workshop Reward Shop with 100 respect (with 150 extra in the upgrade progress) is quite essential to reduce the effort to maintain the cannons. The dwarf multicannon and kinetic cyclone are the Ranged and Melee variant of the cannons respectively. The Oldak coil is a Magic variant which is further recommended to be used instead of the dwarf multicannon, if possible.

Unlocking the dwarf multicannon, kinetic cyclone, and Oldak coil upgrade kits can permanently increase their damage output by 100%, 50%, and 50% respectively.

These are incredibly useful for dark beast and edimmu assignments, as they constantly cycle aggression towards the player whenever they are hit. Most tasks can generally be completed within the duration of the cannon (25 minutes), and even then maintenance is fairly low if it runs out of cannonballs, with a simple click to get it back up and running again. Some areas will prohibit the use of these cannons, so aggression potions should be used in their place if necessary.

There are 3 categories for Summoning familiars that would assist in high-level slayer tasks—Combat, Beasts of Burden, and Healers.

Use of combat familiars like nihil (87 Summoning) or steel titans (99 Summoning) can increase your experience rates. Nihils are only needed for particularly troublesome tasks such as airut and Kal'gerion demons, who possess high defence and low affinity values, as even the best equipment can still miss relatively often. Otherwise, steel titans should be used, as most monsters don't possess fairly high defence levels or low affinity values that would make it troublesome for their accuracy.

Beast of Burden familiars may be used at tasks where the additional inventory can prove helpful, such as ripper demons and camel warriors. Otherwise, magic notepaper should be used to cert drops from monsters such as airut. Pack yaks are incredibly useful for most slayer tasks due to their ability to bank up to 240 items per hour, and adding 30 spaces to the player's inventory to fill with extra supplies and carry loot.

Legendary pets are by far the best option for those who want to make some money off of slayer without hindering their experience rates much. These pets have 3 incredibly useful abilities: Scavenge, Beast of Burden, and Slayer Finisher. The Scavenge ability picks up items after killing enemies with a 10-15 second cooldown. The second ability makes it act as a Beast of Burden when a pouch is used on the familiar. The third ability is for Nechryael tasks for automatic kills if quick kills is not unlocked.

For most assignments, it is the most beneficial to use a Beasts of Burden, for its ability to store valuable loot, and withdraw food and prayer potions, effectively extending trips before needing to restock. Higher level Beasts of Burden last longer and have more inventory slots.

When extra inventory slots are not needed, healing familiars, e.g. bunyip (68 Summoning) and unicorn stallion (88 Summoning) or combat familiars, e.g. Ripper Demon (96 Summoning) and steel titan (99 Summoning) can be used instead.

Quick ways of recharging summoning points include the tribute stone near the Falador lodestone, and the Altar of War in War's Retreat.

You should always use Turmoil/Anguish/Torment to increase your kills per hour. If you can afford them, Malevolence/Desolation/Affliction should be used as they provide greater bonuses. Soul Split, whether constantly active or via prayer flicking, will serve as the "food" for a majority of tasks, negating the need to bring actual food, though a few should be taken for emergencies.

For some tasks, notably dragons, you can use a bonecrusher in conjunction with demon horn necklace. This method negates the need for prayer potions during task. This can also be used with monsters that drop ashes via the use of the attuned ectoplasmator; though it will eat considerable profit due to the cost of ghostly essence.

Holy wrench passively increases the prayer points restored from potions. This includes super prayer, prayer renewal, and super restore potions. The wrench can be worn in the pocket slot to save backpack space.

Players with at least level 99 Slayer can fill their Slayer Codex. It is advised to invest slayer points and time to collect at least 100 different monster souls. For every 20 souls collected, slayer helmets grant a +1% gain (up to 5% at 100 souls) to Slayer experience, effectively being an experience boosting item.
